question: Does a fixed published ten-month equity/cash rule improve drawdown and losing-month frequency beyond simply holding less equity?
scope: Single-ETF SPY/BIL adaptation; not original proprietary-index result replication or a funded account.

frozen_design.signal: Ten completed month-end adjusted SPY closes, fixed SMA10, ties keep prior state.
comparators: Calibration-only mean equity allocation rebalanced monthly
frozen_design.holdings: Synthetic total-return units held between monthly events; no daily rebalancing.
frozen_design.limits: Gross fractional USD accounting; no taxes, commissions, slippage, FX or lot rounding; historical period is not genuinely unseen.

execution.return_or_risk_conclusion: None. Access failure does not validate or invalidate the strategy.

independent_check: Error-body hashes corroborated. Timing source reviewed against separately frozen formulas; no numeric performance acceptance possible.
model_review: Official DeepSeek returned a final critique supporting a calibration-only exposure control and distinguishing same-close idealization from next-open execution. This is design criticism, not performance evidence.
next_gate: Qualify an available historical price/total-return snapshot and corporate-action conventions before one unchanged-rule economic comparison. Preserve this failed attempt.
